oneSentenceSummary: Multiple industry giants fast-tracking direct AI-enabled purchasing signals a structural shift toward platformless, agent-driven commerce that marginalizes traditional branded storefronts.
editorialTake:
Direct AI-driven purchasing is about to break the link between brand and channel, and anyone still thinking of AI as a back-office tool is missing the point. Walmart’s Daniel Danker is calling 2026 the year AI moves from experiments to full-scale transformation, but the real shift is happening in how and where customers buy. Etsy is letting logged-in Google users buy marketplace items straight from Google’s AI Mode and Gemini app, skipping Etsy’s own site. Frasers Group is wiring up Commercetools so shoppers can buy through AI agents like ChatGPT, not just through its own digital storefronts. Google itself is pushing open-source agentic commerce with Shopify, aiming to make the act of buying native to the AI layer, not the retailer’s site.

This isn’t about chatbots or virtual assistants answering questions. It’s about AI agents that can complete transactions, recommend products, and even negotiate or bundle offers, all without the shopper ever seeing your homepage. The latest TCS study finds most retailers see the biggest AI impact in operations, but the front-end is where the power shift is happening. Alibaba is connecting its shopping and travel services to its main AI app, betting that controlling the AI interface means controlling the sale. The platform is no longer your site, it’s wherever the customer’s AI agent happens to be.

Skeptics will argue that luxury and jewellery buyers want the brand experience, not just frictionless transactions. That’s true for high-ticket, emotional purchases, but the AI layer is already capturing the impulse and replenishment sale. If AI agents become the default entry point, even luxury will feel the squeeze on lower-ticket or gifting items.

Operators need to plan for a world where your products are surfaced, recommended, and sold by someone else’s AI. This quarter, test how your catalogue, imagery, and product data perform in agentic channels like Google’s AI Mode and Shopify’s new tools. If your brand story and value proposition don’t travel through these pipes, you risk becoming invisible, no matter how good your store looks.
